/info/about.title: About Vitalii Radov — Digital Designer & Framer Developer
/info/about.description: I'm Vitalii Radov, a digital designer and Framer developer focused on clarity, structure, thoughtful details, and creating better experiences for the web.
h3: The details are never just details
Every project already has a personality
Good structure lasts longer than trends
p: I've always been drawn to things that feel thoughtfully made. A book, a photograph, a piece of music, a website ‒ the medium doesn't matter much. What interests me is the thinking behind it. The decisions, constraints, and attention that shape the final result.

That curiosity eventually became the foundation of my work.  I don't really separate design and structure in my head. When something feels off, it's usually because the structure is unclear, not because the visuals are wrong.

Most of my work is about making things easier to understand ‒ visually, but also in how they're organised and experienced. What goes where, and why it matters. I tend to work toward clarity without adding more than necessary. Just enough so things start to feel inevitable.
People rarely notice clarity itself, but they notice when it's missing. A lot of my work is simply making things easier to understand and navigate.
Spacing, typography, timing, alignment ‒ they're easy to overlook on their own. Together, they're what makes a website feel considered.
I don't try to invent one. Usually it's already there, hidden in the work, the process, or the way someone talks about what they do. My job is to bring it forward.
I like movement that helps things make sense. Not animation for its own sake, but motion that creates rhythm, flow, and a sense that things belong where they are.
Visual styles change. Clear thinking tends to age better. I trust structure more than novelty.
Adding is easy. Deciding what to leave out is usually where the real work begins.
They're very different disciplines on the surface, but I often find myself drawn to the same qualities in each of them: structure, rhythm, simplicity, and attention to detail.
I enjoy understanding how things are put together ‒ how a space is organised, how a photograph is composed, how a product works, or how a system makes complexity feel simple.
Outside of work, you'll usually find me with a camera, cycling, walking through a city, reading, listening to music, or disappearing into a rabbit hole about technology or how something was made.
I enjoy slowing down enough to notice things that are easy to miss ‒ materials, light, texture, form, composition, typography, and the countless small decisions behind everyday experiences.
A lot of what eventually finds its way into my work begins there.
Alongside client projects, I'm working on new Framer templates, refining my approach to design and development, and collecting more references than I'll probably ever need
